title: Princeton PEAR lab and the Global Consciousness Project: random event generators spike on 9/11 and at Bob Jahn's death

tellings.quote: 911 was the biggest spike they've ever seen.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about a Princeton University lab tied to a scientist named Bob Jahn and a related effort that ran machines making random numbers around the world, to see if human feelings could affect them. Michels says the machines showed their biggest spike ever on September 11, 2001, the day of the terror attacks, and another when Jahn died. If true, it would suggest that human minds together can touch the physical world.
